q: What are the emissions from making baker's yeast?
title: Yeast plant emissions
short: Yeast is grown on molasses in aerated fermenters. CO2 released by the yeast comes from sugar, so report it separately as biogenic. Fossil emissions come from aeration blowers and cooling (electricity), steam for sterilising and drying, and effluent treatment.

ul: Air blowers and compressors for aeration.
Steam for sterilising and for drying yeast.

p: Anaerobic effluent treatment can release methane, which counts in Scope 1 unless it is captured and burned.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
